title: Staphylococcus saprophyticus Infection - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf

claims.text: S. saprophyticus is the second most common cause of community-acquired UTIs, after E. coli.
claims.byte_quote: saprophyticus is the second most common cause of community-acquired urinary tract infections, after Escherichia coli

claims.text: In females ages 16 to 25, S. saprophyticus causes up to 42% of all UTIs.
claims.byte_quote: In females ages 16 to 25, it causes up to 42% of all infections.

claims.text: Nearly half of women will have a UTI in their lifetime; in 5%-20% of non-hospitalized patients the infection is due to S. saprophyticus.
claims.byte_quote: Nearly half of all women will experience a UTI in their lifetime, and between 5% and 20% of non-hospitalized patients, the infection will be due to S.

claims.text: Over 40% of young, sexually active women carry S. saprophyticus as part of normal genitourinary flora.
claims.byte_quote: Over 40% of all young, sexually active women contain S. saprophyticus as part of their normal genitourinary flora.

claims.text: S. saprophyticus is a Gram-positive, coagulase-negative, non-hemolytic coccus causing uncomplicated UTIs, particularly in young sexually active females.
claims.byte_quote: Staphylococcus saprophyticus is a Gram-positive, coagulase-negative, non-hemolytic coccus that is a common cause of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs), particularly in young sexually active females.

claims.text: General UTI risk factors: recurrent UTI history, female sex, recent intercourse, pregnancy, neurogenic bladder, indwelling catheter, benign prostatic hypertrophy.
claims.byte_quote: General risk factors for UTIs include the history of recurrent UTIs, female sex, recent sexual intercourse, pregnancy, neurogenic bladder, indwelling catheter, and benign prostatic hypertrophy.

claims.text: Men have a lower incidence of S. saprophyticus infections.
claims.byte_quote: Men have a lower incidence of S. saprophyticus infections.

claims.text: A complicated UTI typically involves a patient who is immunocompromised, elderly, male, pregnant, diabetic, and/or has urologic abnormalities such as indwelling catheters or kidney disease.
claims.byte_quote: A complicated infection typically involves a patient that is immunocompromised, elderly, male, pregnant, diabetic, and/or with urologic abnormalities such as indwelling catheters or kidney disease.

claims.text: Polymicrobial infections are more likely in patients who are immunocompromised, elderly, diabetic, have indwelling catheters, HIV, and/or malignancies.
claims.byte_quote: Polymicrobial infections are more likely to occur in patients that are immunocompromised, elderly, those who have diabetes, have indwelling catheters, HIV, and/or malignancies.

claims.text: S. saprophyticus can be differentiated from another coagulase-negative staphylococcus by its resistance to Novobiocin.
claims.byte_quote: saprophyticus can be differentiated from another coagulase-negative staphylococcus by its resistance to Novobiocin.

claims.text: Like most gram-positive uropathogens, S. saprophyticus does not reduce nitrate to nitrite (negative urine nitrite).
claims.byte_quote: saprophyticus does not reduce nitrate to nitrite.

claims.text: First-line for uncomplicated S. saprophyticus UTI is nitrofurantoin 100 mg orally twice daily for 5 days (7 days if complicated).
claims.byte_quote: saprophyticus UTIs is nitrofurantoin 100 mg orally twice daily for five days, or for seven days in complicated cases.

claims.text: Alternative for uncomplicated cases: TMP-SMX 160 mg/800 mg by mouth twice daily for 3 days.
claims.byte_quote: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) 160 mg/800 mg by mouth twice daily for three days may be given alternatively in uncomplicated cases.

claims.text: Pyridium may be given to alleviate associated dysuria.
claims.byte_quote: Pyridium may also be given to alleviate associated dysuria.

claims.text: S. saprophyticus is resistant to antibiotic regimens commonly used and effective for E. coli UTIs, including ampicillin, ceftriaxone, cephalexin, and ciprofloxacin.
claims.byte_quote: saprophyticus has resistance to antibiotic regimes commonly prescribed and effective for E. coli induced UTIs, including ampicillin, ceftriaxone, cephalexin, and ciprofloxacin.

claims.text: Some strains form biofilms (increasing virulence, especially with catheters); once biofilms form, antibiotic resistance is exacerbated and the organism may be vancomycin-resistant, treatable only via linezolid.
claims.byte_quote: Once biofilms have been produced, antibiotic resistance is exacerbated. In these cases, S. Saprophyticus may be resistant to vancomycin and only effectively treated via linezolid.

claims.text: Patients with nosocomial catheterization have an increased incidence of S. saprophyticus colonization.
claims.byte_quote: catheterization have an increased incidence of S. saprophyticus colonization.
